correctness.rationale: Every S-plant joint extinction probability is exactly q raised to its pollinator-neighborhood union size. Binary-indicator factorial moments show that the first two factorial moments cancel under full labeled pair equality, and the third-central-moment difference equals six times the triple-neighborhood-union polynomial difference. The explicit graph pair has identical labeled degree/pair concurrence signatures, and triple-union histograms (1,3,16) versus (0,5,15), hence 6 q^3 (1-q)^2. Exact exhaustive multiset enumeration (8874 connected incidence multisets at orders 4..10) shows no pair-signature collision with a different triple-union histogram. The script directly evaluates all 32 witness failure states and validates rational moments. The finite conclusion is not extrapolated to unbounded graph sizes.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2004 coextinction primary study analyzes robustness curves under pollinator removal, not exact third central moments with all per-plant/pair loss laws matched. The inspected 2018 knockout-study source analyzes distributions of integrated robustness across extinction sequences and degree-distribution skewness, not the third moment of fixed-probability plant losses. The classical Pasch trade supplies a known pair-balanced mechanism, expressly not claimed new; the 11-total-species sharp cutoff and q-uniform third-central-moment polynomial under connected 3-regular pollinator neighborhoods were not found by the reported scientific searches or in accessible prior claims. Risk remains of a design-theoretic implicit corollary or unseen supplement; no uniqueness certification is asserted.
residual_risks: The design-trade literature might already state an implication equivalent to this exact minimality bound under a non-ecological formulation.

value.rationale: The natural observed one-/two-species joint extinction risks, including the complete mean/covariance information of the loss count for every common failure probability, do not determine third-order tail asymmetry. The result gives the sharp first connected incidence-network size under uniform pollinator degree three and an explicit quantified discrepancy, a useful finite benchmark for identifying genuinely higher-order ecological risk not visible in pairwise data. It is not asserted to model realistic dependent failures or to generalize beyond this well-defined class.
